CVE-2026-114216.title: Chunk extensions accept bare LF and CR, enabling request smuggling in Bandit
CVE-2026-114216.description:
Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling') vulnerability in the HTTP/1.1 chunked body reader of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to smuggle a second request past a front-end proxy via a chunk extension that contains a bare LF.

The chunked reader in lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex takes the chunk-size line to be everything up to the first CRLF and discards everything after ; without checking it against the RFC 9112 chunk-ext grammar, so bare LF, bare CR and other control bytes pass. A proxy that ends the size line at a bare LF reads 2;\nxx\r\n40\r\n... as one request whose second chunk holds a GET /admin, while Bandit ends the body early and dispatches GET /admin as a separate pipelined request. Deployments without such a proxy in front of Bandit are not affected.

This issue affects bandit: from 1.12.4 before 1.14.0.

CVE-2026-116247.title: pgAdmin 4: libpq uses the pgAdmin service account's own password file and client certificate
CVE-2026-116247.description:
When a server in pgAdmin 4 had no password file, client certificate or client key configured, or the configured one could not be found, pgAdmin left the parameter out of the connection and libpq fell back to the defaults of the operating-system account running pgAdmin: ~/.pgpass, ~/.postgresql/postgresql.crt and postgresql.key, or PGPASSFILE, PGSSLCERT and PGSSLKEY. In server mode any user could therefore connect to a server with the service account's saved passwords or client certificate, and supplying only a copy of its public certificate was enough for libpq to pair it with the service account's private key. A pg_service.conf entry, or a maintenance database name read as a connection string by pg_dumpall, could bring the same files back for the utilities.

CVE-2026-124541.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str
CVE-2026-124541.description:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str.

A string is decoded through a fixed-size buffer (16 KiB in 4.04), and each time the buffer fills its contents move into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the string is then rejected for a control character, an invalid escape, malformed UTF-8 or the end of the input.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains the decoded part of each rejected string, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

CVE-2026-61846.title: Crass: Deeply nested CSS blocks and functions can trigger a SystemStackError or excessive memory usage
CVE-2026-61846.description: Crass is a Ruby CSS parser that's fully compliant with the CSS Syntax Level 3 specification. Prior to 1.0.7, Crass recursively parses `CSS simple blocks and functions` without a depth guard. An attacker-controlled CSS value containing deeply nested blocks or functions can recurse until Ruby raises `SystemStackError`: stack level too deep, or cause excessive memory usage. Version 1.0.7 adds a configurable depth limit with a conservative default. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.7.

CVE-2026-63501.title: ag-psd: Uncontrolled Memory Allocation in PSD Layer Decoding (totalMemoryLimit bypass)
CVE-2026-63501.description: ag-psd is a JavaScript library for reading and writing Photoshop Document files. Prior to 31.0.3, readPsd() accepts a totalMemoryLimit for parsing untrusted PSD files, but decodeLayerImageData expects a differently named memoryLimit property and therefore passes an undefined limit to createImageDataBitDepth. An attacker who can supply a PSD to an application with layer decoding enabled can use attacker-controlled layer dimensions to trigger an allocation larger than the configured limit, causing process memory exhaustion and denial of service. The advisory also identifies inflateSync(compressed) decompressing ZIP-encoded channel data without an output-size cap, which can cause a similar denial of service through unbounded decompression. This vulnerability is fixed in 31.0.1.

CVE-2026-98558.title: net: flush skb_defer_nodes in dev_cpu_dead()
CVE-2026-98558.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: flush skb_defer_nodes in dev_cpu_dead()

When a CPU goes offline, dev_cpu_dead() drains its softnet queues
(completion_queue, output_queue, poll_list, process_queue, and
input_pkt_queue), but leaves net_hotdata.skb_defer_nodes untouched.

If oldcpu goes offline while holding pending skbs in its
skb_defer_nodes lists (e.g. below the sysctl_skb_defer_max >> 1 IPI
threshold, or if the IPI races with CPU teardown), those skbs remain
stranded until oldcpu is brought back online. If any of these skbs
hold page_pool fragments, page_pool_destroy() will stall indefinitely
waiting for inflight pages to be returned when a netdev or driver is
torn down while oldcpu is offline.

Additionally, if smp_call_function_single_async() fails in
kick_defer_list_purge() because the target CPU went offline, reset
defer_ipi_scheduled to 0 so future IPI kicks are not blocked when the
CPU comes back online.

keys: Check the authorization payload in process keyring searches

An authorization payload and its saved credentials must remain valid
while search_process_keyrings_rcu() searches the requestor's keyrings.

payload.data[0] and unconditionally reads rka->cred. Validation does
not prevent request_key_auth_revoke() from clearing the payload.

target instantiation invalidates the authorization key without clearing
